source_title: Barbara Barrie’s Daughter Reveals Mom’s Final Day Before Medically Assisted Death (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
Barrie, an actress who appeared in the original production of Stephen Sondheim’s ‘Company’ and TV’s ‘Suddenly Susan’ died at 95 on Wednesday, Oct. 28
Actress Barbara Barrie, who died with medical assistance at age 95 on Wednesday, Oct. 28, spent her final day reading The New York Times and talking with family, says her daughter Jane Harnick
Barrie had long supported medical aid in dying before she was diagnosed with terminal cancer
Barrie made her Broadway debut in 1955 and appeared in Giant , The Twilight Zone and The Fugitive
Actress Barbara Barrie, who died on Oct. 28 at age 95 with medical assistance, had a wonderful last day, according to her daughter Jane Harnick.
“She listened to WQXR every morning, and read the New York Times everyday,” Harnick says. “She read the New York Times on her last day of life. She was up in bed reading the Times , and we were all just talking.”
Harnick says Barrie, who had terminal cancer, felt assured in her decision to die at her home in New York.
“She was ready to go. She was 95. She did everything she wanted to do. She had the family she wanted. She had the house she wanted. She swam in the ocean this past summer. She had a new hip when she was 94.”
The transition couldn’t have been more peaceful. “Literally, our last words to her as she was falling asleep were, ‘We love you,’ and her last words were, ‘I love you.’ And then she was asleep. It was beautiful. It was really beautiful.”
Harnick also says the family was pleased that the Medical Aid in Dying Act had recently been passed in New York, in August.
Stephen Danelian/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty
“My mom had said her whole life, even before she was ever sick with anything, before she had any illness of any kind, that when the time came, she wanted to just take something and go to sleep,” Harnick says, “And so when this last incident happened, when she was pronounced terminal and was at the end of her life, she was so grateful that [Governor] Kathy Hochul had passed this law and made it legal in New York.”
She adds, “She was a huge advocate of it, and she wants it out there that it’s okay to talk about, it’s okay to make this decision, and it’s okay to support the people who want to do this. No matter what your beliefs are, that shouldn’t matter.”
Barrie made her Broadway debut in The Wooden Dish in 1955. In 1959, she appeared in The Beaux Stratagem , and in 1966, she starred in Happily Never After . She then appeared in the 1956 film Giant , a role that came about because she was visiting her family when the movie was filming in Corpus Christi.
But her most significant early career success came on television. Her many TV roles in the ‘50s and ‘60s included episodes of The Defenders , Route 66 , Naked City , Dr. Kildare , The Twilight Zone , The Alfred Hitchcock Hour and The Fugitive . She also starred with Brooke Shields and Judd Nelson on the ‘90s TV series Suddenly Susan.
While Harnick says she’ll always miss her mom, she’s glad that she died peacefully.
“She went out on her own terms, and it was incredibly peaceful,” she says. “It was before any pain kicked in, and she went out with her dignity intact.”
